items.stem: Recording 'room tone' on a location shoot is important because it:

options.text: Provides ambient sound the editor can use to smooth and fill gaps in dialogue
options.rationale: Correct: room tone gives continuous ambience for seamless audio edits.
Room tone is audio, not picture.

options.text: Replaces the need for a boom microphone
options.rationale: It supplements, not replaces, dialogue recording.

items.explanation: Correct: room tone gives continuous ambience for seamless audio edits.

items.stem: Which TWO shots are typically needed to cut together smoothly within a continuity sequence? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A wide (establishing) shot showing spatial relationships
options.rationale: Correct: the wide establishes geography for the cut.

options.text: Matching coverage such as a medium or close-up on the action
options.rationale: Correct: matched coverage lets the editor cut on action.

options.text: A single unbroken take with no other coverage
Random unrelated B-roll with no matching action

items.explanation: Correct: the wide establishes geography for the cut.

items.stem: The '180-degree rule' in filmmaking exists mainly to:

options.text: Keep consistent screen direction so the audience is not spatially confused
options.rationale: Correct: staying on one side of the action line preserves screen direction.
It is about spatial continuity, not exposure.
It concerns camera placement, not sound.
It has nothing to do with duration.

items.explanation: Correct: staying on one side of the action line preserves screen direction.
